chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Discouragement, the Depression, and refusing to copy Bix or Louis
summary: He stuck with music for love of playing, took only a few notes from Bix and Armstrong, and condemns Red Nichols copying Bix note for note.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: of all, - they say - oh, well, you were influenced by Bix anyway---

All right - so I was a little. Maybe a little but I never could play like they do because I was too damn dumb to copy anybody, but I thought if I got a few notes that sounded like Louie that was enough and I used to play kind of Bix ; I remember once a record came up where they thought I was Bix on it, and we talked about that. But, I had a lot of discouragements and, you know, I was with bands that paid so little money and then, getting up to the depression, which was a kick in the face, I remember a guy looked at me - here I am out of work - and he said - well, why don't you come and work for me? And, I said -- what kind of work is that? He said, sell used cars for me--- I said, good-gye.
The thing is - that out of all this, you did develop your own unique style; so that there is a Davison School of Jazz opposed to any other kind of jazz---

Well, as I said - I was too dumb to copy anybody. I didn't want to copy anybody. It used to irk me to no end to hear Red Nichols - make a record and copy Bix note for note. Oh, God - I thought that was sacrilegious - I thought that was terrible for anybody to do that -- and then, there was a guy once I heard a record - called - 'Copying Louie' - and there was some guy that copied Louie note for note and made a record of it. I don't think that's cricket.
And, it's also not real music - is it?
